welcome.title: The densitometry page
welcome.text: Where the bands are measured: each band's area on its lane's profile, its share of the lane, and what the gel's assay reads from it, a purity or a western readout. A short tour; leave it at any time with <kbd>Esc</kbd>.

steps.title: The readout at a glance
steps.text: Sample lanes, bands, lanes analysed, the gel's readout and its calibrations. Then To check: what the readout still lacks, a POI band or a reference lane for instance. Click one for what to do.

steps.title: How a band's % is computed
steps.text: Lane Total: each band as a share of its lane. Loading Control: relative to the lane's MW Reference band, which every lane with bands must carry, or the run is refused. Neither changes the purity. It applies at the next run; the ? beside it explains both.

steps.title: Run the densitometry
steps.text: Measures every band: its area on the lane's profile, background removed, then its % and the gel's readout. Greyed once the analysis is approved: an approved analysis is final.

steps.title: The gel and its bands
steps.text: The gel with the bands you annotated. Click a lane to select it, a band to follow it: the four panels share the selection. The buttons enhance or invert the display, hide the bands, or open the panel full screen.

steps.title: The profile, and the readout's charts
steps.text: Electropherogram: the selected lane's profile, background removed, each band's area filled in its type's colour. Beside it: POI purity or the western readout, as the gel's assay reads, then the quantification curve and a 3D view.

steps.title: Measurements
steps.text: Lanes: one row per lane with the gel's readout, the values the analysis page shows; a missing value says why. Bands: one row per band, its MW, area and % of the lane; a clipped band carries Saturated, a warning that changes no area.

steps.title: Export, report and more
steps.text: Export CSV of the measurements and a Report in Word, Excel or PowerPoint, both once the gel has results. Also the image adjustments, which change the display only, and How densitometry works.
